title: Add geocoding proxy/cache service for Nominatim (replace direct mobile->Nominatim calls)
description:
## Problem

The mobile app currently calls https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org directly from the client to resolve lat/long <-> City/Country. This has several downsides:

- No control over Nominatim's usage policy (max 1 req/sec, requires a valid User-Agent/Referer, no heavy uniform polling) - risk of the app's IP/traffic getting rate-limited or blocked since all requests originate from many individual mobile clients instead of one identifiable backend.
- No caching - repeated lookups for the same City/Country (or the same lat/long bucket) always hit Nominatim again, wasting quota and adding latency for users.
- No observability - we cannot trace, meter, or alert on geocoding calls the way we do for our own services (OpenTelemetry/Prometheus).
- Mobile team is coupled to a third-party API contract directly (shape of Nominatim responses leaks into the app).
- Nominatim/OSM usage policy requires attribution and a proper User-Agent identifying the application - easy to get wrong when called from many client installs, easy to enforce centrally from one backend service.

## Proposed solution

Introduce a new backend service (working name: `location` or `geocoding`) that sits between mobile and Nominatim:

```
mobile -> gateway -> location-service -> nominatim -> location-service -> mobile
```

Responsibilities:
1. Expose our own REST endpoints (via the gateway, following the existing routing/auth pattern in gateway/internal) for:
   - Reverse geocoding: lat/long -> City/Country (and any other fields the app needs).
   - (Optional/forward-looking) Forward geocoding: City/Country -> lat/long, if/when mobile needs it.
2. Proxy requests to Nominatim's API on the backend, setting a proper User-Agent per Nominatim's usage policy and enforcing our own outbound rate limiting (mirroring Nominatim's max 1 req/sec policy) so we don't get blocked.
3. Cache results in PostgreSQL (or Redis, see open questions) keyed by normalized City+Country (and/or rounded lat/long) so repeated lookups for the same location don't hit Nominatim again.
4. Follow existing service conventions from CLAUDE.md "Adding a New Service": DDD layering (domain/application/infrastructure/interfaces), own cmd entrypoint, own migration(s) for the cache table, registered in gateway router, added to docker-compose.yaml, service-specific Prometheus metrics.

## Why this matters / priority

- Direct third-party calls from a mobile client are a latent production risk: if Nominatim rate-limits or blocks our traffic (shared IP ranges, missing/invalid User-Agent, bursty usage), reverse-geocoding breaks for all users with no server-side fallback or visibility.
- This is straightforward to introduce now (before the mobile app has many more direct integration points against Nominatim) and unlocks caching, cost/latency savings, and observability.

## Scope / Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New service scaffolded following existing DDD conventions (domain/application/infrastructure/interfaces + metrics), with its own cmd entrypoint.
- [ ] Endpoint(s) for reverse geocoding (lat/long -> City/Country) exposed through the gateway, following existing auth/routing rules.
- [ ] Outbound calls to Nominatim set a compliant User-Agent and respect Nominatim's usage policy (rate limiting to <= 1 req/sec).
- [ ] Results are cached (DB table or Redis) keyed by normalized location, with a defined TTL/invalidation strategy, so repeat lookups for the same City/Country avoid a new Nominatim call.
- [ ] Service registered in docker-compose.yaml and gateway router.
- [ ] Basic Prometheus metrics for the new service (request counts/latency, cache hit/miss ratio, Nominatim call counts).
- [ ] Mobile team has a documented contract (endpoint + request/response shape) to switch to, replacing their direct Nominatim calls.

## Open questions (to resolve during design/implementation)

- Cache store: shared PostgreSQL table (consistent with "shared DB across services" pattern) vs. Redis (already used for caching elsewhere)?
- Cache key normalization strategy: exact City+Country string match vs. rounded lat/long grid buckets vs. both.
- TTL for cached entries (Nominatim data can change, e.g. new addresses) - or treat City/Country resolution as effectively immutable and cache indefinitely.
- Whether to also cover forward geocoding (City/Country -> lat/long) now or in a follow-up.
- New service name/port and whether it lives under an existing bounded context (e.g. account-profile, since it's used for user location context) or as a standalone service.
close_reason: Location service implemented (commit e233b69): reverse+forward geocoding via gateway, Nominatim UA + 1 req/s limiter, Postgres bucket cache, metrics, compose, swagger and README contract. All acceptance criteria verified in code.

title: ReconstructActivityGroup drops capacity - GetActivityGroupByID always returns nil DefaultCapacity, so group capacity is never enforced
description:
activity/internal/domain/activity_group.go's ReconstructActivityGroup(id, creatorID, title, description, activityType, difficultyLevel, visibility, status, location, timezone, capacity, createdAt, updatedAt, cancelledAt, deletedAt) *ActivityGroup accepts a capacity *Capacity parameter but never assigns it in the returned &ActivityGroup{...} struct literal - the capacity field is simply omitted, so it's left at its zero value (nil) regardless of what's passed in.

activity_group_repo.go's GetActivityGroupByID (and mapActivityGroupModelToDomain) correctly scans default_capacity from the DB and constructs a non-nil *domain.Capacity when the column is non-NULL, then passes it into ReconstructActivityGroup - but that value is silently discarded. Confirmed via a debug test: creating an ActivityGroup with capacity=1 and immediately calling GetActivityGroupByID on it returns group.DefaultCapacity() == nil.

Impact: every capacity check in member_service.go (RequestToJoin's up-front check and ApproveMember's re-check, both guarded by 'if capacity := group.DefaultCapacity(); capacity != nil') is unconditionally skipped for ANY activity group loaded from the database, since GetActivityGroupByID is the only way application code loads a persisted group. This means activity group capacity limits have never been enforced at runtime - not a concurrency bug, a total no-op, independent of the TOCTOU race fixed for group capacity in rekreativko-api-b8q (which cannot even be verified/exercised until this is fixed, since the capacity-check block itself never runs).

Fix: add capacity: capacity, to the &ActivityGroup{...} struct literal in ReconstructActivityGroup.
close_reason: ReconstructActivityGroup was silently dropping its capacity parameter instead of assigning it to the struct, so GetActivityGroupByID always returned nil DefaultCapacity and group capacity was never enforced regardless of concurrency. Fixed by assigning capacity: capacity in the struct literal; verified via a debug test that round-trips a group through create+load.

title: CreateRSVP capacity downgrade is dead code for non-approval 'going' RSVPs
description: In activity/internal/application/attendee_service.go's CreateRSVP, the non-approval 'going' branch calls domain.NewRSVPManualAttendee(session, groupID, userID, status) which sets a.status = status (i.e. AttendeeStatusGoing) immediately, then calls attendee.UpdateRSVP(status, session, confirmedCount) to apply the capacity-aware downgrade-to-pending logic. But domain.Attendee.UpdateRSVP's very first line is 'if newStatus == a.status { return nil // no change }' - since a.status is already Going (set by NewRSVPManualAttendee above) and newStatus is also Going, this check is always true, so UpdateRSVP returns immediately without ever running the hasCapacity check. Net effect: a brand-new RSVP to a non-approval-gated session for status='going' is ALWAYS created as 'going', regardless of session capacity - overbooking every full session's non-approval-gated 'going' RSVP path, independent of any concurrency (this is a sequential logic bug, not the TOCTOU race fixed in rekreativko-api-b48, though it compounds it). The capacity check only actually works today via UpdateRSVP (an existing attendee changing status to going, where oldStatus != Going) and via CreateRSVP's approval-gated branch (a separate HasCapacity check before creating a pending join request). Fix: in CreateRSVP's non-approval branch, create the attendee with an initial status of Pending (or via a status-less constructor) and then call UpdateRSVP(status, session, confirmedCount) to let it decide the real starting status, OR check capacity before calling NewRSVPManualAttendee and pass in AttendeeStatusPending directly when the session is full.
close_reason: Made NewRSVPManualAttendee check capacity itself for status=Going (downgrading to Pending + emitting AutoPendingEvent when full) instead of relying on a follow-up UpdateRSVP call that was always a no-op since newStatus already equaled the just-constructed status. Verified with unit tests that fail without the fix.

title: Gateway API key secret committed in observability/prometheus.yml
description: The real GATEWAY_API_KEY value used to protect service-to-service auth (shared/middleware/gateway_key.go CheckGatewayKey) and the gateway /metrics endpoint (shared/middleware/metrics_auth.go RequireMetricsToken) is hardcoded in plaintext at observability/prometheus.yml:34 (credentials: "468019b5-a863-4e49-b8d8-2c420079ac7b"). This value is identical to GATEWAY_API_KEY / GATEWAY_API_KEYS in the gitignored .env file (.env:28-29), confirming it is the live secret, not a placeholder. The file's own comment (observability/prometheus.yml:26-29) explicitly warns 'in production this file must not be checked in with a real secret inlined - inject it via templating or a secret-mounted config,' but the real secret was committed anyway in commit 36cb6607. Anyone with read access to the git history/repo now has the key that authenticates as the gateway to every backend service (identity, account-profile, activity, notifications) and can also scrape the gateway's own /metrics. Fix: rotate GATEWAY_API_KEY/GATEWAY_API_KEYS immediately, remove the literal value from prometheus.yml (use envsubst/templating at container start, or a Prometheus secret file via file_sd/external secret mount), and scrub the value from git history if feasible.
close_reason: Removed hardcoded GATEWAY_API_KEY from observability/prometheus.yml; switched to credentials_file backed by a Docker Compose secret, rotated the key in .env

title: Mising visibility paramater in CresteSessionRequest
description: Mobile team currently sends two requests to when creating new Sessions. One to create and other to update visibility. We MUST give them option to send visibility in one request and do it in one request. Check if same must be done for update session
close_reason: Added visibility to CreateSessionRequest/UpdateSessionRequest (now required on both), wired through to domain SetVisibility/NewSession, and removed the standalone-must-be-public restriction so standalone sessions can be public or private.

title: Session invitee cannot view a private standalone session before accepting the invite
description: SessionService.GetSession only shows a private session to its creator, attendees or confirmed group members (isSessionRelated). A user with a pending session invite (rekreativko-api-06r) is none of those, so the client can show the invite (which only carries session_id) but cannot fetch the session's title/time/location to let them decide whether to accept. Consider treating a pending, unexpired session invite as 'related' in isSessionRelated (needs SessionInviteRepository in SessionService), or embedding a session summary in SessionInviteResponse. Also check ListSessions/DiscoverSessions visibility.

title: Notifications: handle activity.session_invite.* events
description: Session invites (rekreativko-api-06r) publish activity.session_invite.sent/accepted/declined/expired via the outbox, but the notifications service only subscribes to activity.invite.* (group invites), so an invitee is never told they were invited (only discoverable by polling GET /api/v1/session-invites) and the creator isn't told about accept/decline/expiry. Add subscriber entries + handlers in notifications/internal/interfaces/events (mirror inviteSent/Accepted/Declined/Expired handlers, payload has session_id instead of activity_id), new notification types, and handler tests.

title: Live updates for team formation via SSE (server->client stream)
description:
DECISION: use Server-Sent Events (SSE). Commands (assign, pick, propose, vote, close) stay plain REST; the stream only tells clients that state changed. Mobile team leaned WebSocket (React Native has no built-in EventSource; polyfill needed on native and web) - we chose SSE anyway, revisit WebSocket later if needed (e.g. chat/live scoring). Keep the hub/snapshot design transport-agnostic so switching only touches the last handler.

## Scope
One stream per session carrying ALL team-formation state: captain draft (turns, picks, completed/cancelled), proposals + vote tallies, voting closed / tie needs admin, and team assignment changes (from draft, vote result or direct admin assignment). Does NOT carry RSVPs, attendee joins/leaves or session edits (may be added later).

## Design
- Endpoint: GET /activity/api/v1/sessions/{id}/events, Accept: text/event-stream, normal Authorization header, proxied through the gateway like any other route. Note: browser-native EventSource cannot set Authorization; the RN web build must use a fetch-based SSE client/polyfill.
- Access check on connect: same visibility rule as reading the session (Session.IsVisibleTo / confirmed attendee).
- Every event is a full snapshot of team-formation state (current teams + draft if any + open proposals with tallies). First event on connect is a snapshot, so reconnect = fresh snapshot; no Last-Event-ID replay or delta merging. Include a monotonically increasing id/version so clients can ignore stale snapshots.
- Heartbeat comment line (": ping") every 15-25s.
- Source: outbox -> NATS -> each activity API instance subscribes and fans out through an in-memory hub keyed by session id -> connected clients.
- GET snapshot endpoint returns the same payload (client fallback: poll every 2-3s if SSE misbehaves on a platform).

## Must fix / verify in current code (nothing streaming exists today)
- gateway/cmd/api/main.go:185 http.Server WriteTimeout 15s and activity/cmd/api/main.go:245 WriteTimeout 15s will kill the stream: clear the write deadline per request for this route (http.ResponseController).
- gateway/internal/proxy.go ProxyToService wraps every request in a per-service context timeout (default 30s, ACTIVITY_SERVICE_TIMEOUT): bypass for the stream route.
- Verify middleware chain (metrics, tracing/otelhttp, logging wrappers) preserves http.Flusher / Unwrap so events are not buffered.
- Measure outbox publisher polling interval: it adds to end-to-end latency between a pick/vote and clients seeing it.
- Consider closing/filtering the stream if a user is removed from the session mid-stream.

## Client notes (mobile)
Open only while the draft/vote screen is visible; background delivery is push (separate epic). Client refetches full state on reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: Clients receive team-formation snapshots in near real time through the gateway; heartbeat keeps idle connections alive; reconnect gets a fresh snapshot; unauthorized users rejected; stream not cut by gateway/activity timeouts; tested across multiple API instances

title: Team formation events as in-app notifications
description:
Notifications service consumers for team formation events, delivered through the EXISTING notification pipeline as in-app notifications (verify how in-app delivery works today in notifications/). Push delivery is out of scope here - see the separate push infrastructure epic.

Events: selected as captain, your turn to pick, draft completed, new proposal, voting closed / teams finalized, tie needs admin decision, moved to a team by admin.
Include deep-link data (session id + target screen) in the payload so mobile can route once push exists.
While the app is open, live state comes from the SSE stream (.4); this ticket covers the notification record/feed.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed event creates an in-app notification for the right recipients with deep-link data

title: Captain draft: admin picks two captains, captains alternately pick players
description:
Draft state machine per session.
- Admin/creator picks two captains from joined (confirmed) attendees and starts the draft.
- Turn order + current turn stored; captain may only pick an unassigned confirmed attendee on their own turn (reject otherwise).
- Captains are auto-assigned to their teams. Draft completes when all confirmed attendees are assigned; result written to team_id (replaces previous teams - admin-initiated).
- Admin can cancel a draft; existing teams remain untouched on cancel.
- Edge cases: captain leaves/goes not_going mid-draft, attendee leaves mid-draft, waitlist promotion mid-draft, turn timeout (decide alternate vs snake and timeout).
- Events: draft_started, turn_changed (your turn to pick), player_picked, draft_completed, draft_cancelled.
- Endpoints: start, pick, cancel, GET draft state (full state for client resync).
acceptance_criteria: Draft runs end to end with turn enforcement; concurrent picks are safe; edge cases handled; events emitted; tests for state machine and races

title: Team proposals and voting: suggest a division, vote, admin closes, winner applied
description:
Proposal aggregate + votes.
- Any confirmed attendee can suggest a full division into teams at any time. Suggesting does NOT reset current teams.
- Every confirmed attendee has one vote across proposals and can change it while voting is open.
- Voting stays open until admin/moderator closes it (no deadline, no auto-close).
- On close: the proposal with most votes is applied automatically (written to team_id). On a tie the admin selects the winner (close is rejected/pending until they choose).
- Always possible to submit new proposals after a close (starts a new voting).
- Validation: proposal must cover only confirmed attendees, respect players_per_team, each attendee in at most one team.
- Edge cases: attendee leaves or is promoted from waitlist while proposals are open (invalidate or adjust proposals - decide), open question whether "keep current teams" is an implicit option, archive vs delete after close.
- Events: proposal_created, vote_cast/changed, voting_closed (winner), tie_requires_admin.
- Endpoints: create proposal, vote, close (with optional winner_proposal_id for ties), list proposals with tallies, GET state.
acceptance_criteria: Proposals and voting work end to end; tie resolved by admin; winner applied automatically; re-suggesting never resets teams; roster-change edge cases handled; tests

title: Teams foundation: session team config, session_team table, attendee team_id, volleyball
description:
Base model everything else builds on.
- Add ActivityTypeVolleyball to shared/activitycatalog (+ validity map; check account-profile interests).
- Optional team config on Session and SessionTemplate: team_count (default 2), players_per_team. nil = current behavior. Generated sessions inherit template config.
- Migration 000002: activity.session_team (id, session_id, name, position, created_at); nullable team_id on activity.session_attendee (FK). NULL = unassigned.
- Domain: Team inside Session aggregate; Attendee.AssignToTeam/Unassign. Invariants: only confirmed (going/promoted) attendees, max players_per_team, one team per attendee, slot freed on leave/not_going/removal.
- Direct assign/move endpoint for admin/creator; teams + members in session response DTOs; swagger; update .claude/docs/activity.md.
- Concurrency: reuse advisory-lock approach (lockSessionCapacity); integration test modelled on attendee_capacity_race_integration_test.go.
- Events: attendee.team_assigned / team_changed / team_unassigned via outbox.
acceptance_criteria: Team config on one-off sessions and templates; direct assignment works with per-team limits under concurrency; slots freed on leave/removal; volleyball selectable; non-team sessions unchanged; migration, tests, swagger, docs

title: Activity: team formation for team sports (basketball, football, volleyball)
description:
## Problem
The activity service has no concept of teams. A Session has one flat attendee pool bounded by `capacity`; Attendee has no team field; SessionTemplate cannot carry team config; volleyball is missing from shared/activitycatalog. See child tickets for the breakdown.

## Scope (phase 1)
Team-vs-team sports (basketball, football, volleyball). Tennis/doubles/brackets are out of scope but the model must stay extensible.

## Agreed product decisions
- Current teams (team_id on attendees) persist until replaced. Suggesting a new division NEVER resets existing teams by itself.
- Ways to form/change teams: (a) admin/creator assigns directly, (b) captain draft: admin picks two captains, captains alternately pick from joined attendees, (c) team proposals: any confirmed attendee can suggest a full division, others vote for the one they prefer.
- Voting stays open until the admin/moderator closes it (no deadline, no auto-close).
- On close the winning proposal is applied automatically; on a tie the admin selects the winner.
- Re-dividing is always possible: anyone can submit a new proposal at any time, admin can start a new draft at any time.
- Live updates: server->client only, commands go through REST. Transport (SSE vs WebSocket) to be decided with mobile team; neither exists in gateway/notifications today.

## Open questions
- Is the current division an implicit "keep current teams" option in a vote?
- After a vote closes, are proposals/votes archived or deleted?
- Should captain draft alternate (A,B,A,B) or snake (A,B,B,A)? Turn timeout?
- Should team slots replace session capacity or coexist with it?
- Team names: free text vs fixed (Team A/B, colours)?

## Mobile team dependencies (tickets to be created by mobile team)
Captain selection UI, draft screen (turn indicator, pool, teams), proposal builder, proposals list + voting, team display on session, push/deep links for team events, live-update client (SSE/WebSocket) with resync via GET state.
acceptance_criteria: Team config on sessions/templates for basketball, football, volleyball; team-slot limits enforced under concurrency; slots freed on leave/removal; events emitted; non-team sessions unchanged; migration, tests, swagger and docs updated

title: Mobile: switch to backend forward-geocoding endpoint (drop direct Nominatim call)
description:
The location service now exposes forward geocoding (previously tracked as rekreativko-api-7ul, closed): GET /location/api/v1/geocode/forward via the gateway.

Contract:
- Method/Path: GET /location/api/v1/geocode/forward
- Query params: city (required), country (required), street (optional - switches Nominatim resolution to free-text search for better street-level accuracy)
- Auth: Bearer token required (gateway-enforced, GET only), same as every other authenticated mobile endpoint
- Success 200 body: {"status":"success","message":"","timestamp":"...","data":{"latitude":number,"longitude":number,"display_name":string,"city":string,"country":string,"country_code":string}}
- Errors: 400 invalid/missing city or country, 401 unauthorized, 404 no location found for the query, 502 geocoding provider (Nominatim) temporarily unavailable - all in the standard {"status":"error","error":{"code","message"}} envelope
- Results are cached server-side (normalized city+country+street key), so repeated lookups are fast and don't hit Nominatim again

Why: mobile's web target currently calls nominatim.openstreetmap.org directly for forward geocoding (nominatimForwardGeocode in its location client, used by Session/Session Template location fields to resolve a typed city/street into coordinates). That direct third-party call has no server-side rate limiting, caching, or User-Agent policy compliance - the same problem already fixed for reverse geocoding. Mobile should switch this call to the new endpoint and remove the direct Nominatim dependency.

Reference: location/README.md documents the full API (note: its "Known follow-ups" section is stale and still says forward geocoding isn't implemented - worth a doc fix separately).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Mobile web target's Session/Session Template location fields call GET /location/api/v1/geocode/forward through the gateway instead of nominatim.openstreetmap.org directly
- [ ] Direct nominatimForwardGeocode call/dependency removed from mobile's location client
- [ ] 404 (no location found) and 502 (provider unavailable) handled gracefully in the UI
close_reason: Created in error - mobile team will file their own ticket in their repo based on a plain-text handoff instead.

title: Group join/approval capacity check is the same TOCTOU race as rekreativko-api-b48
description: member_service.go's RequestToJoin (~line 186-195) and ApproveMember (~line 529-541) enforce ActivityGroup.DefaultCapacity() with the same check-then-act pattern that rekreativko-api-b48 fixed for session attendees: CountConfirmedMembers is read, compared against capacity.Capacity(), and only afterwards is the join request/approval written - all inside a plain READ COMMITTED transaction with no row lock or advisory lock. Two concurrent RequestToJoin calls (or two concurrent ApproveMember calls) for the same capacity-limited group can both read the same confirmed count, both pass the capacity check, and both commit - overbooking the group past its stated capacity. Same fix pattern as b48: take a transaction-scoped Postgres advisory lock keyed on the activity_group_id before reading the confirmed count in both RequestToJoin and ApproveMember, mirroring AttendeeService.lockSessionCapacity in attendee_service.go.
close_reason: Added lockGroupCapacity (transaction-scoped Postgres advisory lock, distinct namespace from the session lock) before the capacity check in RequestToJoin and ApproveMember, mirroring the b48 fix for session attendees. Verified with a concurrency integration test (20 attempts of concurrent ApproveMember against a capacity-1 group); also required fixing rekreativko-api-ypt since the capacity check was otherwise unconditionally skipped.

title: Outbox publisher has no horizontal-scale locking and a failing event can permanently block its schema's queue (poison pill)
description: shared/events/outbox_publisher.go's publishFromSchema() reads up to readLimit unpublished events per schema via domainevent.domainEventManager.ReadEvents (shared/domainevent/domain_event.go), which is a plain 'SELECT ... WHERE published_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT ' with no FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and no row-level claim/lease step. Two problems: (1) Horizontal scaling: running more than one outbox-publisher instance (e.g. for HA or to keep up with growing event volume across identity/account-profile/activity/notifications schemas) would let multiple instances read and attempt to publish the same batch of events concurrently, since nothing claims/locks rows before they're marked published - this can produce duplicate NATS publishes beyond what at-least-once delivery already implies, and duplicate/racy MarkEventAsPublished calls. (2) Poison-pill events: publishFromSchema() logs and does  on both Publish() and MarkEventAsPublished() failures, leaving the row unpublished. Since ReadEvents always orders by created_at ASC with a fixed LIMIT and there's no retry-count/backoff/dead-letter mechanism, a single event that permanently fails to publish (e.g. a marshaling issue, or a broker rejecting a specific payload) will be re-selected at the head of every poll cycle forever, permanently occupying one of the readLimit slots and delaying every younger event in that schema indefinitely, with only a repeating error log as a symptom. Suggested approach: add 'FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED' (or an explicit claimed_at/lease column) to ReadEvents to make the publisher safe to run with >1 replica, and add a retry_count/last_error column plus a max-retry threshold that moves permanently-failing events out of the hot path (e.g. into a dead-letter state/table) so they stop blocking newer events. Effort: M.
close_reason: Outbox publisher reads batches in one tx with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (safe for multiple replicas); failures tracked via retry_count/last_error and dead-lettered via failed_at after OUTBOX_MAX_RETRIES. Unit + integration tests added (a301463).

title: RBAC role checks are unwired: JWT carries no roles, RolesContextKey is never set in the gateway auth flow
description: gateway/internal/router.go defines AuthRule.RequiredRoles and Router.hasRequiredRoles(), and shared/middleware/user_context.go's ExtractUserContext reads roles from the X-User-Roles header downstream. But the chain that is supposed to produce those roles is broken end-to-end: (1) shared/token's Claims struct has no Roles field at all, so a JWT can never carry roles; (2) shared/middleware/auth.go's AuthMiddleware.RequireAuth (the gateway's JWT validator) only calls context.WithValue(ctx, authcontext.AccountIDContextKey, accountID) - it never calls authcontext.WithRoles, so authcontext.GetRoles(ctx) always returns []string{} inside the gateway; (3) gateway/internal/router.go's addUserHeaders() therefore always forwards an empty X-User-Roles header to backend services; (4) no Route in loadRoutes() actually sets RequiredRoles today, so the feature is currently 100% dead code with no live callers. This blocks documented admin-only use cases from .claude/docs/arhitecture.md ('Create activity type - admin') and the Activity Group 'admin' role concept from .claude/docs/activity.md. Suggested approach: either (a) decide roles belong on the Account aggregate in Identity and get embedded in JWT claims + propagated through the existing header/context plumbing, or (b) decide authorization is out of scope for now and remove the dead RequiredRoles/hasRequiredRoles scaffolding to avoid misleading future implementers into thinking route-level RBAC already works. Effort: M (if wiring it up), S (if removing it).

title: Session capacity check is a TOCTOU race - concurrent RSVPs/approvals can overbook
description:
Session capacity enforcement in activity/internal/application/attendee_service.go follows a check-then-act pattern with no locking: CountConfirmedAttendees(txCtx, sessionID) is read, then compared via session.HasCapacity(confirmedCount), and only afterwards is the new attendee row inserted/updated - in CreateRSVP's approval-gated branch (count+HasCapacity check before creating the pending request), in UpdateRSVP's going-status path (attendee.UpdateRSVP with confirmedCount), and in the new ApproveAttendee (count+HasCapacity check before attendee.Approve). All of this runs inside a transaction opened with pgx.TxOptions{} (shared/store/postgres/transactions.go BeginTx), i.e. plain READ COMMITTED - there is no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, advisory lock, or SERIALIZABLE isolation anywhere in this path (grep for 'FOR UPDATE'/'Serializable' across activity/internal/infrastructure/persistence and shared/store/postgres finds nothing).

Under READ COMMITTED, two concurrent RSVP/approval requests for the same session can both read the same confirmedCount before either commits its insert, both pass the HasCapacity check, and both commit - overbooking the session past its stated capacity. This directly undermines the capacity/waitlist invariant the domain otherwise cares carefully about (auto-downgrade to pending, waitlist promotion, ErrSessionFull).

Fix direction: take a row lock scoped to the session for the duration of the capacity check + write (e.g. SELECT ... FROM activity.session WHERE id =  FOR UPDATE before the count, or a Postgres advisory lock keyed on session_id), or add a DB-level capacity constraint/trigger that rejects inserts past capacity so the application-level race can't silently overbook even if it loses the check.
close_reason: Added a transaction-scoped Postgres advisory lock (lockSessionCapacity) before each capacity check/write in CreateRSVP, UpdateRSVP, and ApproveAttendee, closing the check-then-act race. Verified with a concurrency integration test that fails without the lock and passes with it.

title: Notifications service has no idempotency guard against NATS at-least-once redelivery
description:
notifications/internal/interfaces/events/handlers.go handlers (e.g. memberJoinRequestedHandler.Handle, and all the others in this file) call notificationCreator.CreateNotification and just insert a new notifications.notification row every time - there is no event_id column or unique constraint tying a notification to the domain event that produced it (see notifications/internal/infrastructure/persistence/migrations/000001_notifications_schema.up.sql, which only has id/recipient_account_id/type/data/read_at/created_at).

The JetStream consumer uses AckExplicitPolicy with a 30s AckWait and calls msg.Nak() on handler error (shared/events/nats_broker.go around lines 101-281), i.e. at-least-once delivery: any transient error (DB blip, pod restart before ack, redeploy) causes the same event to be redelivered and reprocessed from scratch.

This is compounded for fan-out handlers like memberJoinRequestedHandler.Handle (notifications/internal/interfaces/events/handlers.go), which loops over event.ManagerUserIDs and returns immediately on the first CreateNotification error - on redelivery, managers already notified in a previous partial attempt get a second, duplicate notification, and there is nothing anywhere that would ever have deduplicated them even without a partial failure (a clean redelivery of a fully-successful event also creates duplicates).

Impact: users can receive duplicate/spammy notifications for the same event whenever NATS redelivers a message, which will happen periodically in normal operation. Fix direction: add an event_id (or event_id+recipient_account_id) column with a unique constraint on notifications.notification, thread the domain event's ID through CreateNotificationParams, and upsert/ignore-on-conflict in NotificationRepository so redelivery is a no-op.
close_reason: Notifications now store the originating event_id with a unique (event_id, recipient_account_id) constraint; Create uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so NATS redelivery is a no-op

title: CreateRSVP misclassifies member-lookup DB errors as 'not a group member'
description:
activity/internal/application/attendee_service.go CreateRSVP (around lines 100-120) does a membership lookup via memberRepo.GetMemberByGroupAndUser and then does:

switch {
case err == nil && member != nil && member.IsConfirmed():
    isPriorityMember = member.IsPriority()
case session.IsPublic():
    // non-member joining a public session as an attendee only
default:
    log.Error(txCtx, "user is not a group member and session is not public", "error", err)
    return domain.ErrAttendeeNotGroupMember
}

GetMemberByGroupAndUser (activity/internal/infrastructure/persistence/member_repo.go GetMemberByGroupAndUser) returns domain.ErrMemberNotFound for the expected 'not a member' case, but wraps and returns any other error (e.g. a transient DB/connection failure) as a plain fmt.Errorf. The switch above does not distinguish between these: any non-nil err is treated identically. Consequences: (1) for a private session, a real infrastructure error is silently converted into the business error ErrAttendeeNotGroupMember (likely surfaced as 403) instead of propagating/logging as a 500, hiding the actual failure from logs/metrics; (2) for a public session, a real infrastructure error during the membership check is swallowed entirely with no log line at all (the case is chosen solely on session.IsPublic(), ignoring err), and the request silently proceeds as if the user were a confirmed non-priority attendee. Fix: check errors.Is(err, domain.ErrMemberNotFound) explicitly and propagate any other error immediately instead of folding it into the public/private branching.
close_reason: CreateRSVP now propagates non-ErrMemberNotFound member lookup errors instead of treating them as not-a-member

title: Private standalone sessions have no invite/attendee-add mechanism
description: A private standalone session (no activity_group_id) can now be created/updated as private (see rekreativko-api-h9r), but there's no way for anyone other than the creator to become an attendee. CreateRSVP rejects self-RSVP for a private session unless the requester is a confirmed group member or the session is public; a standalone session has no group at all, so only the creator (auto-attendee on creation) can ever attend. GroupInvite/SendInvite only works against activity_group_id, so it can't be used for a standalone session either. Need a session-level invite or direct attendee-add mechanism (e.g. creator invites specific users to a private standalone session) so private standalone sessions are actually usable beyond a party of one.
close_reason: Added session-level invites (accept/decline) for standalone sessions: SessionInvite aggregate, session_invites table, service, endpoints, cron expiry, tests, docs

title: Fix failing SessionTemplateRepository integration tests (location_city NOT NULL)
description: Pre-existing on main (verified on clean HEAD): go test -tags=integration ./activity/internal/infrastructure/persistence fails 7 TestSessionTemplateRepository_* tests (CreateAndGet, Update, Delete, Query, FindRecurringTemplatesToGenerate, UpdateGeneratedUpTo, ConcurrentAccess) with 'null value in column location_city of relation session_template violates not-null constraint (SQLSTATE 23502)'. The SessionTemplateBuilder fixtures don't set location by default (locationCity/locationCountry are nil pointers) while the schema requires them.

title: Device token registration API (notifications service)
description: Table + endpoints to register/update/unregister a device push token per account and device (platform, token, last_seen). Unregister on logout. Routed through the gateway; auth required.
acceptance_criteria: Mobile can register and unregister tokens; multiple devices per account; tokens removed on logout

title: Push delivery via provider (notifications service)
description: Decide provider (Expo push service vs FCM/APNs). Sender consumes notification events, sends to all of a user's devices, handles receipts, retries, and removes invalid tokens. Respect existing notification preferences if any.
acceptance_criteria: A notification event results in a push on registered devices; invalid tokens cleaned up; failures observable via metrics/logs

title: Mobile push notification infrastructure
description:
Platform feature, not team-specific. Neither backend nor the mobile app has push today: the app has no expo-notifications or push setup, and the notifications service only has an SMS sender. Team formation ships without it (live updates via SSE while app is open); push adds background delivery for e.g. "your turn to pick".

Backend scope: device-token storage + register/unregister API, provider integration (decision needed: Expo push service since the app is Expo, vs FCM/APNs directly), sender that turns notification events into pushes, receipt/invalid-token handling.
Mobile scope (their tickets): permissions, token registration, foreground/background handling, deep links.
Once done, team formation notifications (rekreativko-api-6gg.5) can also be pushed.

title: account-profile: treat 'profile exists' as idempotent success when account.verified event is redelivered
description:
account-profile/internal/interfaces/events/account_verified_handler.go creates the profile and settings in one transaction. account_profile.profiles has account_id as PRIMARY KEY, so a redelivered identity.account.verified event hits a unique violation, which is mapped to ErrAccountProfileExists (profile_exists conflict). The handler returns that as an error, so the broker Naks and redelivers up to MaxDeliver=3, then Terms the message and logs errors. No duplicate data is written (the tx rolls back), but a normal at-least-once redelivery is reported as a failure and produces error noise and wasted retries.

Fix direction: in createProfileEventHandler.Handle, treat ErrAccountProfileExists (and the equivalent settings conflict) as success (log at debug and return nil), or make CreateAccountProfile/CreateSettings use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Careful that a partially-existing state (profile exists but settings missing) is still repaired - check both independently rather than swallowing all conflicts. Add a unit test with fakes for redelivery, and an integration test if the repository SQL changes.

Found while checking other consumers after fixing the notifications idempotency bug. Effort: S.

title: NATS consumers drop messages after MaxDeliver=3 with no dead-letter path
description:
shared/events/nats_broker.go configures durable consumers with MaxDeliver: 3 and AckWait 30s. When a handler fails and max deliveries is reached, the message is Term()'d (around lines 252-276) with only an error log. There is no dead-letter stream/subject, no persisted record of what was dropped, and no replay mechanism. Any event whose handler fails 3 times (e.g. a DB outage longer than the redelivery window in notifications or account-profile) is permanently lost, so users silently miss notifications or never get an account profile created.

This is the consumer-side counterpart of the outbox poison-pill fix (rekreativko-api-tqr), which dead-letters on the producer side via retry_count/failed_at. Idempotent handlers (rekreativko-api-m8j) make redelivery safe but do not prevent loss after the third failure.

Design questions: (a) publish terminated messages to a DLQ subject/stream (e.g. dlq.<subject>) with the original payload, error and delivery count, (b) add a redelivery BackOff instead of the fixed AckWait so transient outages outlast 3 attempts, (c) metrics/alert on terminated messages, (d) a way to replay from the DLQ. Distinguish permanent errors (decode failures - Term immediately, straight to DLQ) from transient ones (retry with backoff). Effort: M.
close_reason: Added DLQ stream (dlq.>) in shared/events/nats_broker.go: messages are dead-lettered with failure headers after max deliveries or on permanent errors (decode failures marked via events.Permanent), retries use NakWithDelay, metric events_dead_lettered_total. Unit + real-NATS integration tests. Follow-up hardening in rekreativko-api-755.

title: Introduce interfaces for concrete dependencies in application services so they can be unit tested
description:
Application services depend on the concrete *postgres.TransactionManager (shared/store/postgres), so service methods like AttendeeService.CreateRSVP cannot be unit-tested with mocked repositories without a real database. Found while fixing rekreativko-api-yd6 (no test could be added). Related to rekreativko-api-tf6 (no unit tests for activity domain/application layer) - this is a prerequisite for it.

Scope: go service by service and replace concrete types with small consumer-side interfaces (defined in the application package). Main offender is *postgres.TransactionManager, used as txManager in: activity application (attendee, session, session_template, session_generator, invite, member, activity_group services), account-profile application (account_profile_service, account_settings_service) and events handlers (account_verified_handler, subscriber), identity application/service.go, notifications application/notification_service.go, and shared/domainevent/domain_event.go. Some services also call txManager.Querier(ctx) directly (e.g. AttendeeService.lockSessionCapacity runs pg_advisory_xact_lock), so that needs to be abstracted behind an interface method or a separate locker port. Also audit each service for other concrete deps (*metrics.Metrics, *logger.Logger, telemetry) that block testing.

Suggested approach: define a minimal TxManager interface (WithTransaction(ctx, func(ctx) error) error, plus Querier if unavoidable) - ideally once in shared - have the concrete postgres.TransactionManager satisfy it, and add a fake for tests. Do it per service in separate commits, starting with activity (attendee_service, session_service). Persistence-layer repos can keep the concrete type (they need real DB integration tests). Effort: M-L.

Acceptance: application services accept interfaces for tx manager; at least one unit test per service using mocked repos + fake tx manager proves it works (e.g. CreateRSVP membership lookup error propagation from yd6).

title: Investigate ClickHouse adoption for the project
description: A senior engineer should investigate how ClickHouse could be used in this project and for what use cases (e.g. analytics/reporting, event/metrics storage, large-scale read-heavy query workloads currently served by PostgreSQL). Deliverable: an assessment of concrete use cases where ClickHouse would be a good fit here, how it would fit into the existing architecture (modular monolith with shared PostgreSQL, NATS event-driven communication, outbox pattern), and a recommendation on whether/where to adopt it.

title: Add forward geocoding (city/country/street -> lat/long) to location service
description: The location service (rekreativko-api-bog) currently only implements reverse geocoding. Mobile's web target still calls Nominatim directly for forward geocoding (nominatimForwardGeocode in its location client, used by Session/Session Template location fields to resolve a typed city/street into coordinates) - that direct third-party call is not yet covered by the new backend proxy/cache. Follow-up: add a forward-geocoding endpoint (structured city+country search, plus free-text search when a street is given) to the location service, mirroring the caching/rate-limiting approach already built for reverse geocoding, so mobile can drop its last direct Nominatim dependency.
close_reason: Added forward-geocoding endpoint (GET /api/v1/geocode/forward) to the location service, mirroring reverse-geocode caching/rate-limiting: structured city+country search, free-text search when street is given, Postgres cache table, shared Nominatim rate limiter, new unlabeled cache-hit/miss counters (no cardinality risk), swagger docs regenerated.

title: Shared Config struct forces every service to supply env vars for unrelated services, undermining independent deployability
description: shared/config/config.go defines one flat Config struct embedding ServiceConfig, GatewayServiceConfig, IdentityServiceConfig, AccountProfileServiceConfig, ActivityServiceConfig, NotificationsServiceConfig, Outbox, NatsConfig, JWT, etc., and every service binary (gateway, identity, account-profile, activity, notifications, outbox-publisher/cmd/worker) calls the same config.Load() which runs envconfig.Process("", &c) against the entire struct. Several fields are marked required:"true" globally regardless of which service actually uses them, e.g. GatewayServiceConfig.GatewayKeys (env GATEWAY_API_KEYS - only meaningfully used by the gateway binary to build its outbound X-Gateway-Key value) and Outbox.Schemas (env OUTBOX_SCHEMAS - only used by outbox-publisher/cmd/worker). Because envconfig.Process fails fast on any missing required field, this means e.g. the identity service cannot start without GATEWAY_API_KEYS and OUTBOX_SCHEMAS set in its environment, even though identity's own code never reads either value. This directly contradicts CLAUDE.md's stated architecture ('Each service can run independently...') and adds operational friction: every new required field added for one service's config leaks into every other service's required environment, and it's easy to forget which fields are actually load-bearing for a given binary. Suggested approach: split Config into a small shared 'common' struct (Service, Logger, Server, Postgres, Redis, JWT, Telemetry - the genuinely cross-cutting concerns) plus per-binary structs that each cmd/*/main.go loads separately (e.g. config.LoadGateway(), config.LoadIdentity()), so each service's required env vars match what it actually needs. Effort: M (touches every cmd/*/main.go).

title: Root CLAUDE.md Service Structure section is stale - omits activity (the CORE domain) and notifications services
description: The 'Service Structure' section of the root CLAUDE.md only lists Gateway (8080), Identity (8081), Account Profile (8082), and the Outbox Publisher. It does not mention the activity service (which .claude/docs/activity.md calls out as the 'CORE part of the application', with its own cmd/api and cmd/cron entry points, ~24k lines including migrations, and the largest domain/application layer in the repo) or the notifications service (which has its own full DDD layer set and is routed by the gateway in gateway/internal/router.go and gateway/cmd/api/main.go's serviceConfig map). Same gap in the 'Adding a New Service' checklist and the general architecture description, which still describes only a 3-service-plus-outbox topology. Anyone (human or agent) reading CLAUDE.md to get an overview before working in this repo will miss that activity and notifications exist at all, contradicting the instruction to 'get an overview first' - the doc that's supposed to enable that is itself incomplete. Suggested approach: update the Service Structure list to include activity (8083?) and notifications (8084?) with their actual ports/responsibilities, and mention activity/cmd/cron (the session-template generation cron job) since it's a distinct deployable not covered anywhere in CLAUDE.md's Development Commands section either. Effort: S (documentation only).

title: Application layer repository interfaces depend on infrastructure/persistence Filter types (inverted dependency), plus dead duplicate Filter types in identity
description: Across all three services (identity/internal/application/service.go, account-profile/internal/application/account_profile_service.go, and all of activity/internal/application/*.go via repositories.go), the application-layer repository interfaces are defined against filter/query DTOs that live in the infrastructure/persistence package (e.g. persistence.AccountFilter, persistence.RefreshTokenFilter, persistence.VerificationCodeFilter), and every application file imports .../internal/infrastructure/persistence directly to reference them. In a hexagonal/DDD layering, the application layer should own the port (interface + its parameter types) and infrastructure should depend on application, not the reverse - here the dependency arrow points the wrong way, and it's consistent enough across all three services that it looks like an intentional convention rather than an accident, but it still means application code can never be compiled/tested without pulling in the concrete persistence package. Separately, identity/internal/application/service.go additionally defines its own AccountFilter, RefreshTokenFilter, and VerificationCodeFilter structs (lines ~47-59) that appear to be unused dead code - grep shows zero references to application.AccountFilter etc. anywhere in the codebase, while the interfaces actually in use (accountReaderWriter.GetBy, refreshTokenReaderWriter.GetTokenBy, etc.) take the persistence.* versions instead. Suggested approach: move the Filter DTOs into the application package (or a shared query-params location each service owns) so infrastructure implements against application-defined ports; separately, delete the unused duplicate Filter structs in identity/internal/application/service.go once confirmed unused, or wire them up if they were meant to replace the persistence ones. Effort: M (touches all three services' repo interfaces and their infra implementations).

title: Public-route allowlist for gateway auth is defined twice and can drift
description: The set of unauthenticated identity endpoints (login/register/verify-account/resend-verification-code/refresh-token) is hardcoded as a regex in two independent places: (1) gateway/cmd/api/main.go's publicPaths slice, consumed by middleware.NewAuthMiddleware(...).RequireAuth which runs first in the middleware chain and short-circuits auth entirely for matches; (2) gateway/internal/router.go's loadRoutes(), inside the '/identity' Route's AuthRule with RequireAuth:false, consumed later by Router.isAuthSatisfied. Both lists already differ in content (main.go's list also includes /swagger/.* and /health, router.go's doesn't need to since those aren't proxied routes) which makes it easy to lose track of which list is authoritative. Because AuthMiddleware runs before the router in the chain, router.go's AuthRule.RequireAuth:false is currently mostly redundant/defense-in-depth, but that isn't documented anywhere, so a future contributor adding a new public endpoint could easily update one list and not the other - either accidentally leaving a route behind auth that should be public, or (worse) believing a route is protected because it's marked RequireAuth:true in router.go when AuthMiddleware already let it through unauthenticated. Suggested approach: derive one list from the other (e.g. have main.go build publicPaths from router.NewRouter()'s routes instead of a separate literal), or extract the identity public-path regex into one shared constant/var referenced by both call sites. Effort: S.

title: Domain layer in identity and account-profile depends on infrastructure (pgx) and app-layer concerns (domainerror), unlike activity
description: identity/internal/domain/errors.go and account-profile/internal/domain/errors.go both import github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 directly and implement MapErrToAppError(err error) *domainerror.AppError inside the domain package - mapping domain sentinel errors to an HTTP-status-aware AppError DTO and even special-casing the infra-specific pgx.ErrNoRows sentinel. This violates the DDD dependency rule documented in CLAUDE.md (domain should not depend on infrastructure/interfaces) and couples the domain package to both a specific SQL driver and an HTTP-facing error shape. Notably this is inconsistent across the three services: activity does this correctly - its equivalent MapErrToAppError (and the pgx import) lives in activity/internal/application/error_mapper.go, in the application layer, not domain. Suggested approach: move MapErrToAppError out of identity/internal/domain/errors.go and account-profile/internal/domain/errors.go into a new identity/internal/application/error_mapper.go and account-profile/internal/application/error_mapper.go respectively (mirroring activity's existing pattern), keeping only the plain errors.New(...) sentinels and any pure-domain error types in the domain package. Effort: S per service (mechanical move + import fixups).

title: No unit tests for activity domain/application layer (core domain)
description: activity/internal/domain and activity/internal/application have zero *_test.go files (find activity/internal/application -name '*_test.go' and find activity/internal/domain -name '*_test.go' both return nothing), despite the activity bounded context being called out in .claude/docs/activity.md and CLAUDE.md as the CORE domain of the system. Commit 36cb6607 added substantial, intricate business logic here with no accompanying tests, e.g.: capacity-aware RSVP with waitlist promotion and approval-gated join requests (activity/internal/application/attendee_service.go CreateRSVP/ApproveAttendee/promoteNextPending), session visibility rules mixing public/private/group-membership/attendee checks (session_service.go GetSession/isSessionRelated, ListSessions filter building), session cancellation with attendee fan-out (resolveSessionAttendeeUserIDs), and the cron-driven ExpireCompletedSessions. These paths have subtle edge cases (capacity race re-checks, waitlist ordering, visibility fallback logic) that are exactly the kind of logic regressions slip into silently without tests. Suggest adding table-driven unit tests for the domain invariants (activity/internal/domain/*.go) and service-level tests (with repo interfaces mocked) for the application layer, starting with attendee_service.go and session_service.go given their size and complexity.

title: Access log now logs full raw query string on every request
description: shared/middleware/logging.go's Logging middleware was changed in commit 36cb6607 to add "query_params", r.URL.RawQuery to the structured fields logged on every request (see the 'fields := []any{...}' block). This logs the entire raw query string verbatim for every request at INFO/WARN/ERROR level, with no allowlist/redaction of sensitive parameter names. There is currently no endpoint that puts secrets in a query string, but nothing prevents one being added later (e.g. a password-reset or magic-link GET endpoint with a token=... param, or a search endpoint that echoes free-text PII), and it would then be silently written to logs (which may be shipped to Loki/long-term storage per observability/loki/loki-config.yaml) without anyone noticing, since the middleware is generic and applies everywhere. Suggest redacting known-sensitive query keys (token, code, password, secret, key) before logging, or documenting query strings as an explicit no-secrets zone enforced by review.

title: Broker: harden dead-letter publish failure path (retry DLQ publish, log payload, alert)
description:
Follow-up to rekreativko-api-wpn. In shared/events/nats_broker.go, deadLetter() publishes a failed message to the DLQ stream once. If that publish fails (NATS flap, stream misconfigured), the failure is logged with the stream sequence and counted in events_dead_lettered_total{dlq_published="false"}, and the message is still Term()'d. The payload is NOT in the log; the message is only recoverable from the EVENTS stream by sequence (nats stream get EVENTS <seq>) while it is inside EVENTS retention (7 days / 1GB).

Improvements (a DB table was considered and rejected: handlers usually fail because the DB is down, so a DB fallback would fail in the same outage, and it would add a DB dependency to the shared broker plus a table/migration per service):
1. Retry the DLQ publish 2-3 times with a short delay before giving up, to cover brief NATS flaps. Keep it bounded so a dead broker cannot stall the consumer loop.
2. On final failure, log the payload (truncated) together with the stream sequence, so the message can be reconstructed after EVENTS retention expires. Decide whether payloads are acceptable in logs (events mostly carry IDs but may contain user data); redact or hash if not.
3. Add a Prometheus alert rule (observability/) on events_dead_lettered_total{dlq_published="false"} > 0, since it means the safety net failed and the 7-day recovery window is running.
4. Extend the unit test with a fake DLQ that fails N times then succeeds.

Known related gap, not covered here: if a consumer crashes on every delivery, the server exhausts MaxDeliver without processMessage running, so nothing reaches the DLQ; catching that needs a subscription to the $JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MAX_DELIVERIES advisory.

Only worth a durable store beyond this if the events become business-critical; then prefer a transactional inbox table written by the handler in the same tx as the business change. Effort: S.

title: Activity Catalog bounded context is a hardcoded shared enum, not the documented admin-managed aggregate
description: .claude/docs/arhitecture.md documents a dedicated 'Activity Catalog Context' with its own aggregate (ActivityType: name, description) and use cases ('List activity types', 'Create activity type - admin'), explicitly 'does not know about users, groups and events'. The actual implementation instead defines activity types as a closed, hardcoded Go enum in shared/activitycatalog/activity_type.go (ActivityType string constants + a validActivityTypes map), consumed directly by both account-profile's interests and activity's groups. There is no database table, no admin CRUD API, no per-type metadata (description, icon/category, locale strings), and no way to add or retire an activity type without a code change and redeploy of every service that imports shared/activitycatalog. This works fine at the current small, fixed list size, but it's a real extension point implied directly by the existing docs and code structure (the comment in activity_type.go even says 'single source of truth ... shared across bounded contexts', i.e. it already plays the catalog's role, just without persistence or admin management). Suggested approach: if/when the activity type list needs to grow or vary by market/locale, promote shared/activitycatalog into a real small service (or a table owned by one existing service, e.g. activity) with a simple admin-only CRUD endpoint, keeping the shared Go package as a typed client/cache in front of it rather than the source of truth. Effort: L (new bounded context) - flagging as an opportunity, not urgent, since the current static list satisfies today's needs.
